texts: good. the full-moon state is reified so the date can anchor on it, and the flat copular atom is kept beside it, so both "was the moon full?" and "when?" resolve. One caveat you cannot write around: the calendar terms assume a day-of-month under a month, so "day 47 of Year 1" lands as a bare (Day 47) beside (Year 1) with nothing marking it as a day-of-year - a translator-side gap, not a phrasing problem.
good. one convening event with the Council as agent and "at the Watch" as its location, and the Council stays a single collective participant rather than being spread over unnamed members.

mixed: the report itself is handled correctly - non-factive, with holder and addressee in place and the complement sealed so nothing inside it is asserted as fact - but "fourteen weeks of winter supply" is a measure-of phrase the instruction set does not cover, so the quantity has to be improvised onto a dimension no word in the clause states (and the same phrasing lands on a different dimension in other passages, so the two records will not match each other at query time). Put the fourteen weeks on a verb that names the dimension: "Sailsworn reported to the Council that the winter supply in the salt-bloom store would last fourteen weeks."

good. the issuing is a transfer with the Council as agent, the Station as recipient and the ration as the thing transferred; the three-word premodifier stack resolves mechanically - genus "ration", the adjective "standard" exposed, the noun modifiers "winter" and "feather" left inside the symbol - so no rewrite is needed to shorten it.

good. the continuation state carries the "remained" marker, the "of wraiths" complement rides that state, and the whole report stays sealed with only the Lantern's own identity projected out - exactly the non-committal record you want for a report.

mixed: same measure-of problem as sentence 3 - the report seal and the roles are right, but "eight weeks of supply" has no licensed encoding, so the eight weeks lands on an invented dimension slot and will not line up with the same phrase elsewhere. Rewrite as "Tessa Brae reported to the Council that the supply in the feather store would last eight weeks."
good. the past copular wraps the property atom, and the store is correctly recognized as the same one Tessa Brae's report named, so the two sentences attach to one symbol.
good. a second, distinct issuing event with its own ration witness, so it does not collide with the standard winter ration of sentence 4.

bad: "the stations of the West Row" is an of-genitive, but the parse heads it with the containment relation, which is licensed only for "in / at / inside / within" - so it asserts a spatial containment your sentence never states. If the stations really do sit in the Row, say so outright: "The Council issued an extra feather ration to the stations in the West Row." If instead the Row is the set they belong to rather than a place, "the West Row stations" records the association without claiming containment.
